rv.q: Viewers hoping for a complex mystery and a dazzling display of Holmes’ deductive prowess will be disappointed by the skimpy plot, which is resolved before it really picks up steam.
This is perfect light entertainment for holiday visitors.
At less than an hour long, the show is like a beautifully decorated Christmas cookie—sweet, satisfying and just the right size.
“Sherlock Holmes and the Christmas Clowns” has everything needed for a terrific holiday treat.
As a warm seasonal cup of retro cheer to provide a break from the hubbub of the season, Sherlock Holmes and the Christmas Clowns hits the sweet and silly spot.

One of the other guests at this house party is a notorious international thief. When a godparent’s priceless present is stolen during a holiday play pantomime, can Sherlock discover the culprit before the curtain falls?
For audiences seeking a playful twist on a classic detective during the holiday season, this production offers an entertaining escape.
Delightful, fun, but underdeveloped, “Sherlock Holmes and the Christmas Clowns” is a good play with music that could have been truly great.

cn.t: Critics praise this charming holiday mystery for its witty dialogue, expert lead performances, and delightful blend of Victorian atmosphere with Christmas caroling and light comedic mischief.
